column1: sweden-2025-6|G|Tiling & dissection,Angles|For which integers $n\ge3$ can a regular $n$-gon be cut into exactly $2025$ regular polygons, with no unused area? The smaller polygons need not all have the same shape.

sweden-2024-1|N|Equations & systems,Extremal arguments|Red, blue and white beads each have positive integer weights in grams; beads of the same colour weigh equally. sweden-2023-1|A|Equations & systems|With $30$ km left in a journey, Anna and Lisa share one bicycle. Anna first cycles while Lisa walks. Anna later leaves the bicycle and walks; Lisa takes it when she reaches it and cycles until she catches Anna. They repeat this procedure and arrive together. Anna walks at $4$ km/h and cycles at $15$ km/h; Lisa walks at $5$ km/h and cycles at $20$ km/h. How long do the final $30$ km take, ignoring changeover time?

Find the unknown bag's contents, the total and the allocation.

sweden-2008-2|N|Diophantine equations,Divisibility & GCD|Find the least $n\ge3$ for which two distinct numbers chosen from $1,\ldots,n$ have product equal to the sum of the remaining $n-2$ numbers. Identify the chosen pair.

norway-2026-1(a)|N|Squares & powers,Extremal arguments|Find all positive integer pairs $(a,b)$ such that both $a^2+2b+1$ and $b^2+2a+1$ are perfect squares.

norway-2026-2(b)|C|Invariants,Algorithms & constructions|Orient each unit edge of an $m\times n$ grid in one of its two directions. A move rotates one cell and its four edge arrows by $90^\circ$, leaving all other arrows fixed. Two orientations are equivalent if a sequence of moves transforms one into the other. Determine the largest size of a family of pairwise inequivalent orientations, for positive $m,n$.

norway-2025-3(a)|G|Cyclic quadrilaterals,Coordinates & vectors|In triangle $ABC$, let $E,F$ be the altitude feet from $B,C$. Let $P,Q$ be the perpendicular projections of $B,C$ onto line $EF$. Prove $EP=FQ$.

norway-2024-4(b)|G|Cyclic quadrilaterals,Concurrency & collinearity|A cyclic pentagon has vertices $P_1,\ldots,P_5$. Let $I_i$ be the incentre of $P_{i-1}P_iP_{i+1}$, with indices taken cyclically. denmark-2025-1|A|Equations & systems|Georg puts some coins on a table; his mother then adds twice that many. Georg adds enough to make his cumulative contribution twice hers, and she next adds enough to make her cumulative contribution twice his. Finally Georg adds $240$ coins and his cumulative contribution is again twice hers. How many coins did he put down initially?

denmark-2025-2|N|Modular arithmetic,Binomial coefficients|Start with the six digits $4,a,b,c,4,9$, where $a,b,c\in\{0,\ldots,9\}$. Replace each adjacent pair by the last digit of its sum to obtain a row of five digits; repeat until one digit remains. Which final digits are possible?

denmark-2025-4|G|Circles & tangency,Coordinates & vectors|Inside a large semicircle, a diameter-$4$ semicircle rests on the left end of its diameter and bulges upwards. The configuration is shown below. Find the large semicircle's diameter.\n\n![The three semicircles, with small diameters 4 and 6](assets/range-restoration/denmark-2025-4.png)

denmark-2024-1|N|Modular arithmetic|A miracle number is obtained from a positive integer by adding $3$, multiplying by $4$, adding $5$, then multiplying by $6$. A wonder number is obtained by multiplying by $3$, adding $4$, multiplying by $5$, then adding $6$. Show $318$ is a miracle number but not a wonder number. Can any number be both?

denmark-2024-2|G|Area & dissection,Similarity & congruence|Square $ABCD$ has side $20$, and $P,Q,R,S$ are the midpoints of $AB,BC,CD,DA$. denmark-2026-1|N|Digits & bases,Counting|Distinct nonzero digits $A,B,C,X,Y$ satisfy the decimal subtraction $ABC-CBA=1XY$. How many assignments of the five digits are possible?

denmark-2026-2|C|Graph theory,Equations & systems|Write a real number in each circle of the diagram, with $101$ already assigned at the top. Each circle's number plus the numbers in all circles touching it must have the same total. Is the number in the circle marked $?$ determined? If so, find it.\n\n![Circles with equal closed-neighbourhood sums](assets/range-restoration/denmark-2026-2.png)

denmark-2026-3|N|Valuations,Parity|For $n>1$, reduce all fractions $1/n,2/n,\ldots,(n-1)/n$ to lowest terms and let $f(n)$ be the sum of their resulting numerators. Determine whether $f(2^{1001}\cdot1001)$ is even or odd.

iceland-2026-2|A|Equations & systems|Three taps have constant flow rates and temperatures. Red and green together fill a tub in $70$ minutes at $41^\circ$C; red and blue in $42$ minutes at $35^\circ$C; green and blue in $35$ minutes at $39^\circ$C. Assuming ordinary volume-weighted mixing without heat loss, what temperature results when all three fill the tub together?

iceland-2026-5|G|Circles & tangency,Angle bisectors|From a point $P$ outside a circle $\Gamma$, draw tangents touching it at $A,B$. Prove that the incentre of triangle $ABP$ lies on $\Gamma$.

What is the least $K$ which guarantees eventual capture regardless of the initial positions? Capture means some officer occupies the robber's vertex. All players use optimal strategies.
